newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Thirty-two babies die in Brazilian hospital.
newsitem.headline: Thirty-two babies die in Brazilian hospital.

text.p: Thirty-two babies died during a 20-day period in a Brazilian hospital, victims of what appears to be poor hygiene, officials said on Thursday.
"Unfortunately, it appears the cause of the deaths were infections picked up in the hospital," Health Minister Adib Jatene told reporters.
The deaths occurred during October at the Our Lady of Nazareth Hospital in the city of Boa Vista, capital of remote Roraima state on Brazil's border with Venezuela.
"We sent report after report about the terrible quality of services provided," Odete Domingues, who resigned as the hospital's director on Wednesday, told Globo television.
Globo said daily power cuts of up to 18 hours each sometimes forced surgeons to work by candlelight and said the hospital, which registers about 600 births a month, had only 270 beds.
"I found an ant crawling about the incubator and when I asked to have it cleaned I was told that was normal," the mother of a prematurely-born baby told the television station.
Investigators closed off the maternity unit of the hospital on Thursday.

The tragedy in Roraima is the latest to beset Brazil's ailing health sector. Nearly 100 elderly people died in a private geriatric hospital in Rio de Janeiro between April and July this year as a result of bacterial infections.
And more than 60 people were killed by suspected contaminated water in a kidney dialysis centre in the town of Caruaru, Pernambuco state, earlier this year.
